summary_paragraph: A man with a history of systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, COPD, hepatitis C, and alcohol dependence was admitted for acute shortness of breath and volume overload after again missing his heart failure medications. He had gained nearly 30 pounds since his last discharge and showed signs of fluid retention. A chest X-ray revealed mild pulmonary vascular congestion and cardiomegaly, and his proBNP was markedly elevated. He received IV furosemide and was monitored for alcohol withdrawal, with a peak CIWA score of 15. He declined staying for electrolyte monitoring but agreed to follow-up. He was discharged home on his baseline heart failure regimen with strong counseling to adhere to medications and avoid alcohol.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Other and unspecified alcohol dependence, unspecified
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
